candidates.title: 트리의 성질
candidates.concept_granularity: single set of constraints that make a structure a tree - exactly one root, no cycles, exactly one parent per node - and the consequences, that it stores nothing in sequence and so is nonlinear, that it is recursive because every node heads a subtree, and that it is therefore hierarchical

candidates.title: 힙
candidates.concept_granularity: single special shape of the binary tree - every level filled from the left with no gaps, which fixes the height at the logarithm of the count - ordered so that one extreme sits at the root, which is what makes finding the largest or the smallest constant and keeps every change logarithmic

candidates.title: 큐
candidates.concept_granularity: single restricted structure in which what entered first leaves first - additions at the back, reads and removals at the front, each in constant time, which is the whole of its interface

candidates.title: 스택
candidates.concept_granularity: single structure allowing insertion and removal at one end only, so the last thing in is the first out - one of the restricted structures alongside the queue and the deque - and although the underlying array could be read at any position, doing so is outside what the structure offers, since the problems it solves need only push, pop and a look at the top

candidates.title: 연결 리스트
candidates.concept_granularity: single structure storing with each element the location of the next one, so the elements need not sit together in memory - and which, like the array, keeps its elements in an order, unlike the tree, graph and hash structures that do not

candidates.title: 그래프
candidates.concept_granularity: single structure made of points and the lines joining them, where a line may carry a number and a point's degree is how many lines touch it - a count that splits into arriving and leaving once the lines have direction

candidates.title: 사이클과 연결 요소
candidates.concept_granularity: single set of properties that describe a graph's shape - whether a walk can return to where it began, whether every point is reachable from every other, and how many separate groups the points fall into when only the lines are followed

candidates.title: 인접 행렬과 인접 리스트
candidates.concept_granularity: single choice between the two representations, decided by which question is asked more often - the table answers whether two given points are joined in one step but takes space for every pair including the ones that are not, while the per-point lists answer what a point is joined to in the length of its own list but must be walked to answer the first question

candidates.title: 인접 행렬
candidates.concept_granularity: single representation as a square table indexed by both endpoints, so a connection is one array access and listing a point's neighbours means scanning its whole row, at the cost of space proportional to the square of the point count

candidates.title: 인접 리스트
aliases: 공간은 정점 수 더하기 간선 수
candidates.concept_granularity: single representation holding, for each point, a list of what it joins to - so the space is the point count plus the line count rather than the square, listing a point's neighbours costs exactly its degree, and testing one specific pair costs the smaller of the two degrees

candidates.title: 깊이 우선 탐색
candidates.concept_granularity: single traversal that goes as deep as it can and backs up when it cannot go further, written as a function that calls itself on each unvisited neighbour and returns when there are none - which needs a record of what has already been seen, or the walk repeats itself, and which touches every point and line once

candidates.title: 너비 우선 탐색
candidates.concept_granularity: single traversal that visits everything one step away before anything two steps away - achieved by pushing each newly reachable point onto a first-in-first-out queue and taking the next from the front, which touches every point and line once

candidates.title: DFS와 BFS의 성능 차이
candidates.concept_granularity: single comparison between the two traversals - both visit every point and line so their complexity is identical, and the recursive one runs marginally slower in practice only because of what each call costs, a difference too small to choose on

candidates.title: BFS로 최단거리 구하기
candidates.concept_granularity: single consequence of visiting in order of nearness - everything pushed while processing a point at distance k sits at distance k plus one, so the traversal itself computes shortest distances; and the single condition on it, that every line cost the same, since otherwise the nearest point in hops need not be the cheapest to reach

candidates.title: 다익스트라 알고리즘
candidates.concept_granularity: single algorithm giving the cheapest route from one chosen point to every other - each line examined once and the ordering maintained by a priority queue, or in a plain loop at the cost of the square of the point count - and its one hard limit, that a negative cost breaks the argument it rests on, since it commits to the smallest value found so far

candidates.title: 다익스트라가 도는 순서
candidates.concept_granularity: single loop the algorithm runs - every distance starts at infinity except the source at zero, the nearest unsettled point is taken from a minimum heap and its distance is thereafter fixed, and each of its neighbours is lowered to the taken distance plus the line cost when that is smaller; repeated until the queue empties

candidates.title: 플로이드-워셜 알고리즘
candidates.concept_granularity: single algorithm computing the cheapest route between every pair at once, by asking of each pair whether going through some third point is shorter - three nested loops, so the cube of the point count, which beats running the single-source algorithm from everywhere only when the graph is dense, and whose loops must be ordered with the intermediate point outermost

candidates.title: 경유지를 하나씩 늘려간다
candidates.concept_granularity: single update rule repeated once per possible intermediate point - for every ordered pair, if reaching the first from the second by way of that intermediate costs less than what is recorded, record the smaller; done for the first point, then the second, and so on through all of them

candidates.title: 최소 신장 트리
candidates.concept_granularity: single object - the cheapest way to join every point using as few lines as possible, which is a tree because joining n points without a cycle takes exactly n minus one lines - and the fact that two different algorithms may return differently shaped answers whose total cost is nevertheless identical

candidates.title: 유니온 파인드
candidates.concept_granularity: single structure answering which group an element belongs to and merging two groups - held as one array in which each position records its parent, everything starting as its own parent and so its own group, which is what makes it the standard test for whether joining two points would close a cycle

candidates.title: find와 union이 하는 일
candidates.concept_granularity: single pair of operations - the lookup climbs from an element to its parent repeatedly until it reaches one that is its own parent, which is the group's representative; and the merge finds both representatives and points one at the other, so the two groups become one

candidates.title: 경로 압축
candidates.concept_granularity: single optimisation that keeps the lookup from degrading to a walk of the whole chain - while climbing to the representative, every node passed is repointed straight at it, so the next lookup on any of them finishes immediately

candidates.title: 크루스칼 알고리즘
candidates.concept_granularity: single way of building the cheapest spanning tree from the lines outward - sort them by cost and take each in turn, merging the groups of its two endpoints unless they are already the same group, in which case taking it would close a cycle; the sort dominating the cost

candidates.title: 언제 사이클이 생기는가
candidates.concept_granularity: single test for whether a line may be taken - joining two points already in the tree closes a cycle and joining one that is not adds to it, which is why the line-first algorithm has to check group membership and the point-first one never does

candidates.title: 프림 알고리즘
candidates.concept_granularity: single way of building the cheapest spanning tree from a point outward, which is the single-source shortest-path algorithm with one line changed - what is recorded per point is not the distance from the start but the cost of attaching that point to what has been built so far, so the line cost is compared alone rather than added to the running total

candidates.title: 프림이 도는 순서
aliases: 최솟값을 뽑는 것이 곧 MST에 추가
candidates.concept_granularity: single loop the algorithm runs - taking the point with the smallest attachment cost from the priority queue means adding that point, and the line it was cheapest through, to the tree; then every neighbour of it is lowered to that line's cost when that is smaller, and the whole thing repeats

candidates.title: 위상 정렬
candidates.concept_granularity: single problem of putting tasks in an order that respects which must come before which, where several valid orders usually exist and the algorithm returns one of them - solvable either by the deep traversal or by counting arriving lines

candidates.title: DFS로 위상 정렬하기
aliases: 더 못 갈 때 스택에 넣는다
방문 안 한 정점마다 다시 시작
candidates.concept_granularity: single method taking the order from the traversal's return path - a point is pushed onto a stack when the walk from it can go no further, so popping the stack yields a valid order - with the catch that the walk has to be restarted from every point not yet visited, or a disconnected part is missed

candidates.title: 진입차수로 위상 정렬하기
candidates.concept_granularity: single method that reads the order directly off the arriving-line counts - a task with nothing left before it is one that can start now, so those go into the queue, and taking one out lowers the count of everything it points at until that too reaches zero; and the two graphs it cannot be run on, the one with no direction and the one with a cycle, because neither defines an order

candidates.title: 사전순으로 가장 앞선 위상 정렬
candidates.concept_granularity: single variation that picks a particular one of the valid orders - swapping the plain queue for a priority queue makes the smallest available index come out first at every step, which is exactly the lexicographically earliest order
